purpose: Authoritative-vendor delta adding MachineMetrics, Sight Machine and Poka as manufacturing integration targets at spec-verified only. Reuses existing REST/GraphQL/webhook/database/SCIM profiles, records least-privilege and customer-value boundaries, and does not enable writes or promote any tenant evidence.

systems.name: MachineMetrics
systems.evidenceNote: MachineMetrics documents cloud REST, a read-only GraphQL API and signed webhooks. The REST key model includes read-only reporting/manager.read scopes alongside mutative ERP/operator/manager/gateway scopes, so WFM prefers the natively read-only GraphQL surface or reporting/manager.read keys for data acquisition. Standard and GovCloud endpoints are distinct and must be bound per tenant. Webhook receivers must validate the vendor signature/shared secret and tolerate duplicate, out-of-order and burst traffic. The documented MCP server is not treated as a normal connector surface and remains behind the global agent-action gate. No sandbox or tenant credentials were used.

requiredPermissions: prefer the documented read-only GraphQL API where its data coverage is sufficient
otherwise use a dedicated REST key limited to reporting and/or manager.read rather than ERP, manager, operator, gateway or system.gateway scopes
bind Standard versus GovCloud endpoint explicitly and isolate keys per company/location
validate webhook signature/shared secret and do not grant WFM workflow/webhook-management authority
dataAvailableOrExpected: production metrics including OEE, total/good/rejected parts, cycle time, setup time, downtime and utilisation
real-time machine status and machine/operation/work-order context
shift, operator, job-operation and machine groupings where present in the customer's production model
production activities with actual parts, cycle time, machine, operation and work-order identifiers
event-driven machine-status, downtime, alarm and operator-context notifications through webhooks
automationOpportunities: refresh labour-demand and redeployment recommendations from actual machine state, cycle progress and downtime
identify paid-idle and overtime periods against actual OEE, production output and line availability
use shift/operator/job groupings as evidence for labour-to-output and labour-to-order attribution without making MachineMetrics the worker master
trigger human-reviewed maintenance/staffing responses from signed downtime or alarm events
use overlapping polling plus webhook deduplication so missed or burst events cannot leave workforce decisions stale
savingsHypotheses: reduce avoidable overtime and paid idle time by aligning staffing decisions with actual machine availability and cycle progress
improve labour standards and forecasting using observed cycle, setup and downtime patterns instead of schedule assumptions alone
reduce manual production-to-labour reconciliation using machine, shift, operator and work-order context
reduce custom integration effort by reusing a documented cloud API/webhook path rather than connecting WFM directly to each machine
dataGaps: MachineMetrics is not the authoritative source for employment contracts, absence, payroll, broad skills or agency-worker master data
operator identifiers and work-order semantics require customer-specific reconciliation to HCM/WFM/ERP identities
multi-location examples use separate API keys, so global company/site identity must be reconciled explicitly
REST endpoint permissions and GraphQL field coverage must be proven against the customer's subscription and tenant
constraintsRisks: REST exposes mutative scopes alongside read scopes, so scope inspection is mandatory before authentication evidence advances
GraphQL is documented read-only but has request, execution-time, nesting and node limits that require query budgeting
webhooks can arrive duplicated, out of order or in bursts and have no vendor-side event-delivery rate limit assumption
Standard and GovCloud endpoints must never be auto-swapped across a tenant boundary
MCP/AI tool access is a separate agent authority and remains disabled by default
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing GraphQL, REST/OpenAPI and signed-webhook profiles. In an authorised MachineMetrics environment, bind Standard or GovCloud explicitly, prove a reporting/manager.read key and the read-only GraphQL surface, test GraphQL limits plus REST pagination/time ranges, validate webhook signature/replay/dedupe/burst handling, reconcile site/machine/operator/work-order identifiers, and normalize representative production/downtime/shift observations before promotion beyond spec verification.

systems.name: Sight Machine Manufacturing Data Platform
systems.evidenceNote: Sight Machine documents enterprise integrations through API, SDK or ODBC. Its ODBC service uses the customer sightmachine.io domain, PostgreSQL wire/JDBC/ODBC, tenant_storage and an API key/secret; its in-product APIs also use tenant API credentials. FactoryTX can run locally, on an appliance/VM or Kubernetes and is an ingestion/edge-management surface, so WFM does not operate FactoryTX or receive plant-network authority. Production/workspace database schemas can change as workspaces are published, archived or restored, so schema fingerprints and mapping drift checks are required. No tenant was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: dedicated tenant API key/secret limited to the approved read surfaces available in the customer deployment
read-only ODBC/JDBC access to the customer tenant_storage/sightmachine or approved workspace schemas when database access is used
no FactoryTX configuration, edge API-key management, ingestion or workspace publication authority
tenant/domain binding must be explicit and credentials isolated per customer
dataAvailableOrExpected: contextualized manufacturing models including cycles, downtimes, parts/lots, defects, raw data and KPIs/OEE where deployed
cycle count/time, downtime start/end and fault/root-cause context where modelled
workspace and production-schema data exposed through ODBC/JDBC
dashboard/API values exposed by the customer's enabled API surface
automationOpportunities: use contextualized machine/line state and cycle progress to refresh labour-demand recommendations
correlate downtime and fault context with staffing, maintenance coverage and overtime outcomes
use defects/parts/lot context to identify quality-driven rework labour and qualification demand
reuse machine/facility semantic models to accelerate multi-site work-centre mapping
combine OEE/KPI and labour data for shift-level cost-to-output and executive reporting
savingsHypotheses: reduce paid idle time and avoidable overtime by aligning labour recommendations with contextualized production state
reduce manual multi-site mapping by reusing the platform's facility, line and machine model
reduce quality-related labour waste by linking defect/rework context to the qualified labour deployed on the shift
reduce bespoke historian/MES extraction effort where Sight Machine already provides a governed contextualized data layer
dataGaps: worker contract, absence, payroll, agency and authoritative qualification records normally remain in HCM/WFM/LMS systems
available models and field semantics depend on customer pipelines, workspaces and deployed data products
public documentation does not establish the exact least-privilege scope model for every API/ODBC tenant configuration
workspace publication and lifecycle changes can alter exposed schema objects
constraintsRisks: ODBC production/workspace schemas can drift as models or workspaces are published and must be fingerprinted before mappings are trusted
API key/secret credentials must be vaulted and rotated; least privilege must be proven in the authorised tenant rather than inferred
FactoryTX and edge-key management are ingestion/management-plane functions and remain outside WFM authority
customer transformations can make data derived rather than raw, so provenance, source time, quality and transformation identity must be retained
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST and database-readmodel profiles. In an authorised Sight Machine tenant, prove the minimum read-only API and/or ODBC credential, enumerate the tenant/facility/workspace model, fingerprint production and workspace schemas, validate pagination/query limits and schema-change detection, preserve derived-data provenance, and normalize representative cycle/downtime/defect/KPI records before promotion beyond spec verification.

systems.name: Poka Connected Worker Platform
systems.evidenceNote: Poka's current vendor documentation confirms an open RESTful API, SCIM 2.0 provisioning, webhooks/event triggers, Data Lake/BI integration and Poka Automate. It identifies developer integration domains including users, skills, work instructions, forms and production data, and documents multi-site attributes such as job title, department, manager and site through SCIM. Public material does not enumerate the exact REST authentication/scopes/rate limits, so those remain an explicit sandbox-evidence requirement. MCP and bidirectional/no-code actions are treated as agent/management/write surfaces and remain disabled in the WFM data plane. No tenant was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: dedicated tenant read credential limited to the users, skills, work-instruction/form metadata and production data needed by WFM once exact vendor scopes are proven
SCIM read access may be used for identity/team reconciliation; SCIM provisioning/deprovisioning remains separately write-gated
webhook/event receiver authentication and replay protection must be proven before event-driven use
no Poka Automate, MCP, content publication or cross-system write authority in the normal read connector
dataAvailableOrExpected: users and groups/teams with site, department, manager and job-title context through documented identity integration
worker skills, competency/training completion and certification/expiry context where exposed to the customer API/data products
work instructions, forms and frontline operational records exposed by the documented REST API
production/frontline event data and standardized data-lake models where enabled
webhook/event notifications for configured frontline changes
automationOpportunities: enrich the WFM skill matrix with frontline training/competency evidence and certification expiry context
recommend only appropriately trained/qualified workers for a line or task after customer qualification policy is applied
reconcile users, teams and sites against HCM/WFM identity to reduce duplicate administration
trigger retraining or supervisor review when a required skill/certification is approaching expiry
combine frontline production/issues/forms context with shift outcomes to identify coaching and process-improvement opportunities
after separate write certification, automate approved SCIM lifecycle and training synchronization without granting those rights to the read connector
savingsHypotheses: reduce supervisor time checking spreadsheets or local matrices for who is trained and qualified
reduce avoidable line disruption from expired or missing qualifications by surfacing eligibility before assignment
reduce duplicate worker/team administration by reconciling SCIM and frontline identity with HCM/WFM masters
reduce onboarding and refresher-training administration by linking WFM demand to existing frontline learning evidence
dataGaps: public documentation does not expose exact REST authentication, endpoint scopes, pagination or rate-limit contracts
Poka skills/training evidence must not automatically become legal/work eligibility; customer qualification policy remains authoritative
employment contract, payroll, absence and agency-worker truth normally remain outside Poka
exact customer data-lake/API schemas and which frontline objects are licensed/enabled must be tenant-proven
constraintsRisks: Poka advertises bidirectional API, Automate and MCP capabilities; all action-capable surfaces remain separately gated
SCIM is inherently write-capable even though WFM's initial use is read/reconciliation only
REST authentication and least-privilege scope details are not sufficiently public to advance beyond spec verification without an authorised environment
training completion is evidence, not automatic authorisation to perform regulated or safety-critical work
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST, SCIM and signed-event profiles without enabling provisioning/actions. Obtain authorised Poka developer documentation or sandbox credentials, prove the exact REST auth/scope/rate-limit model and read endpoints for users/skills/training/frontline data, validate SCIM tenant/group/site mappings and webhook authenticity/replay behavior, then normalize representative qualification/training evidence while preserving the customer eligibility-policy gate.
